clue.text: Overbearing poet gets disc manufactured

indicators.note: things manufactured are made up from raw material, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A domineering poet has a record pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotic ruler is tyrannical and domineering, the synonym meaning of overbearing.

clue.text: Beloved one involved in bloodstained rising

indicators.note: one thing involved in another is wrapped up inside it, so a letter goes into the middle
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: something bloodstained is coloured red
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A loved one is caught up in a bloody uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RED into DER, and 'involved in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear is the everyday adjective for someone loved or cherished.

clue.text: For that reason, the prosecutor calls for fizzy water

parts.note: so means therefore, for that reason
a DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Thus the lawyer in court asks for a glass of sparkling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated water, the fizzy kind used as a mixer.

clue.text: King of the Fairies, in the main a sober one

indicators.note: the answer sits in the main body of the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: The fairy king is, for the most part, a temperate fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but signals letters lying within 'a sober one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the King of the Fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: It's meaningless in character so long as it's about tin

parts.note: a sign is a written character or symbol
if means provided that, so long as

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes around it, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Something is pointless if it all revolves around tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's about tin' reads as idle chatter, but 'about' is the container signal wrapping one piece round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insignificant is trivial, of no importance, so meaningless in effect.

clue.text: Queen, known to be dead, wrapped in British flag

indicators.note: one piece wrapped in another sits inside it

parts.note: Queen Anne's dead is an old British saying for stale news, so the queen meant is Anne

explanation.surface: A dead monarch's coffin is draped in the Union flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Anne's dead' is an old British retort to someone announcing news everyone already knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag or standard carried on a pole.

clue.text: Rebuke had Simon reeling

indicators.note: something reeling staggers about dizzily, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Simon is staggering after a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone is to reprimand them, a synonym of rebuke as a verb.

clue.text: Carelessness of new companion starting to open dressing gown

indicators.note: the pieces open up the dressing gown by being put inside it

parts.note: a negligee is a light dressing gown

indicators.note: the starting letter of companion is used

explanation.surface: A new partner begins to undo a dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to open' puts N plus C (from 'starting') between the last two Es of NEGLIGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligence is failure to take proper care, a synonym of carelessness.

clue.text: Earth on limb in part that makes footballers go down

indicators.note: the first pieces go in the word for part

parts.note: a ration is a portion or share

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Earth is put on a leg in some section of a football story.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above; the definition describes being sent down a division.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation sends a football club down to a lower division.

clue.text: Nowadays, clothed and buttonholed

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era
dressed means clothed

explanation.surface: A modern person is dressed and wearing a flower in the lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttonholed' looks like wearing a buttonhole flower; it means accosted.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to stop and speak to them, as is to address them.

clue.text: Will, a deed half-completed, needing an ending

indicators.note: only half of the word deed is done, its first two letters

parts.note: a termination is an ending

explanation.surface: A last testament, only half done, still needs a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' suggests a testament, but here it is resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Will in the sense of resolve or firmness of purpose is determination.

clue.text: VIP to carry honour back

indicators.note: back means both words are read in reverse, right to left

parts.note: to lug is to carry something heavy
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: An important person carries an award home.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful magnate, a very important person.

clue.text: Enduring wish to retain support

indicators.note: something retaining another holds it inside

parts.note: a longing is a yearning wish
a stand is a support

explanation.surface: A lasting desire still keeps hold of something to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: Longstanding means having existed for a long time, so lasting or enduring.

clue.text: Guns by hill going off in confusion

indicators.note: guns going off fire wildly, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Guns fire near a hill amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' looks like the anagram signal but is the definition; 'going off' rearranges GUNS BY HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something blushingly means with embarrassment, which is being in confusion.

clue.text: A guard with passion on show

parts.note: fire is ardour, passion
to screen a film is to show it

explanation.surface: A sentry is shown full of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A firescreen is a guard placed in front of a fireplace.

clue.text: Long to ventilate hideout

parts.note: to air a room is to ventilate it

explanation.surface: Wanting to air a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a verb, to yearn, but it is the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den, or a person's hideout.

clue.text: Democrat leader is given to characteristic cheek

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
a respect is a particular feature or aspect, as in 'in this respect'

explanation.surface: A party chief is prone to typical insolence.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is impudence, a lack of respect, so disrespect is a synonym.

clue.text: Head of aquarium to check market for water

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to dam a flow is to check it
a sale is a market for goods

explanation.surface: The aquarium's boss looks over the fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: ADAM'S ALE is a jocular old name for plain water, the first man's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous phrase for drinking water, since Adam had nothing else.

clue.text: Unusually simple diet for drivers to keep to

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange plain diet is advised for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed limit is the maximum road speed that motorists must stay within.

clue.text: Eastern Church has nothing to imitate

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: The Orthodox Church has no wish to copy others.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to repeat or imitate what they say.

clue.text: Rudeness is unimportant

definitions.meaning: a snub, a piece of rudeness

explanation.definitionFit: Slight is both a noun for a snub and an adjective for something minor.

clue.text: Nearly means a Bible story, which is unrivalled

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, its last letter is dropped

parts.note: one's means are one's income
a parable is a story told by Jesus in the Bible

explanation.surface: An almost unmatched Bible tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of INCOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Incomparable means beyond comparison, without equal, so unrivalled.

clue.text: Sign is functioning, keeping me concealed

indicators.note: something keeping another holds it within itself

parts.note: a machine that is on is working, functioning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A signal is working while hiding my identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: A kind face

definitions.meaning: in printing, a typeface is called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Type means a sort or class, and in printing a typeface.

clue.text: King George with letter written in Greek for little Margaret

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The king writes a Greek letter to a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta is a pet form of the name Margaret.

clue.text: Unknown object makes stomach almost turn inside

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: tummy is an informal word for stomach

indicators.note: almost the whole word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to hinge is to turn on a pivot

explanation.surface: Something mysterious makes one's stomach nearly churn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the verb sense, to pivot on something; 'almost' drops its final E before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy is a whatsit, a word for an object whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Rodney could be in that place

indicators.note: could be means the letters are a possible rearrangement of the name

explanation.surface: Perhaps that's Rodney over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word for over there, in that place.

clue.text: Refer to in policy

parts.note: taken as written
a stance is a position or policy on an issue

explanation.surface: Mention it in the official line.
explanation.definitionFit: To instance something is to cite it as an example, to refer to it.
